misconceptions.description: Assuming any rough surface automatically reduces drag
misconceptions.trigger: learner treats texture as universally beneficial without discussing scale or orientation
misconceptions.feedback: Biomimetic drag reduction depends on geometry, scale, and flow conditions. Some textures reduce drag, while others increase losses if they disrupt the boundary layer poorly.

misconceptions.description: Focusing on biological material instead of hydrodynamic geometry
misconceptions.trigger: learner proposes copying shark skin chemistry rather than the denticle-inspired pattern
misconceptions.feedback: In engineering transfer, the useful abstraction is usually the flow-shaping geometry and how it modifies the boundary layer, not the biological material itself.

misconceptions.description: Assuming only large-scale shape matters in fluid drag
misconceptions.trigger: learner ignores micro-scale surface effects near the wall
misconceptions.feedback: Macro-shape matters, but micro-scale surface features can also influence drag by reshaping near-wall flow and vortex behavior.
